assumptions: AIS-1 bonded identity can be modeled as an accountable agent identity surface with sponsor-backed status.
Delegation, runtime authorization, and provenance remain out of scope for the current AIS-1 substrate and must be composed separately.
prohibitedInferences: Do not infer action-level delegation from bonded identity alone.
Do not treat tier labels as protocol-independent proof of operational trustworthiness.
Do not collapse sponsor accountability into a full relying-party authorization grant.
comparisonNotes: Use this binding to compare AIS-1 with other trust systems without inflating what tier or bond state prove.
validationHints: Check that downstream uses preserve sponsor visibility, tier meaning, and revocation-aware state.
Reject any mapping that upgrades bond existence into blanket delegated authority.
